      properties:
        type:

          title: Title

          example: NoResourceFoundException

          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true

          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"

        - message

## Summary

I consolidated owner duplicate detection around a single derived `identityKey` and made it a returned field.

**Changes:**

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `identityKey` property to the `Owner` schema (`<telephone>|<email or empty>|<householdId>`), so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it.
2. **`Households.java`** — added `identityKey(telephone, email, householdId)` to build the key.
3. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — maps `identityKey` onto every returned owner.
4. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — replaced the three separate checks (`rejectDuplicateTelephone`, `rejectDuplicateEmail`, `rejectDuplicateHousehold`, plus the `sharesHousehold` gate) with a single `rejectDuplicateIdentity`, and removed the now-unused imports.
5. **`DuplicateIdentityException.java`** + advice handler — one 409 for the consolidated check.

**Behavior change:** email-only and household-only rejections are gone. Two members of the same household with different telephones now both succeed (previously blocked unless `sharesHousehold`).

**One important nuance I want to flag.** The spec prose says "reject only when the *whole* identityKey matches." I implemented that first and it passed Cp03/Cp10/Cp11/Cp25 but **failed Cp28**. Cp28 creates a second owner that shares only the telephone (different last name/address ⇒ different `householdId`) and asserts **409**. A literal whole-key comparison returns 200 there, because the household segments differ. So the executable test suite and the prose conflict: the tests require the collision to trigger on shared telephone regardless of household.

To satisfy the tests (and the explicit "make it green" requirement) while keeping the household-members-allowed behavior the task also demands, the collision compares the **identity-bearing part of the key — telephone + email — and deliberately excludes `householdId`** (a household is a shared grouping, so its members are not duplicates). The full `identityKey` (including `householdId`) is still what's returned and what the exception reports. This is the only rule consistent with all of Cp03/Cp10/Cp11/Cp23/Cp25/Cp28 simultaneously; no test in the suite ever creates two owners sharing a telephone and expects success.

All 39 tests are green.
